body.statement:
Uniformly over every compact subset of
\(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times[-\overline h,\overline h]\),
\[
\frac{\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})}{\sigma}
\xrightarrow{p}x_\star(\eta,h)-h\mu_a\mu_b.
\]
The exact phase classification is
\[
x_\star(\eta,h)=h\mu_a\mu_b
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
|h|\leq h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta).
\]
If \(|h|>h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\), then the minimizer lies strictly between zero and the ATT coordinate in its signed direction:
\[
0<x_\star(\eta,h)<h\mu_a\mu_b
\quad\text{when }h\mu_a\mu_b>0,
\]
and
\[
h\mu_a\mu_b<x_\star(\eta,h)<0
\quad\text{when }h\mu_a\mu_b<0.
\]
The set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\) is relatively open in
\(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times[-\overline h,\overline h]\), and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\neq\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\overline h>\min_{\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}}h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta).
\]
No assertion is made for \(|h|>\overline h\).
body.justification: This is the exact local ATT-absorption phase law, including the critical selection and the necessary-and-sufficient reach condition for nonemptiness.
body.gap: The strong-signal endpoint does not identify the bounded rectangular threshold or the selected transition path.
body.consumer: It tells the full-sample enterprise-zone IFE workflow exactly when treatment-supported heterogeneity remains in the coefficient and when fitted factors absorb part of it.
body.proof_tex:
The target and normalized coefficient definitions give the exact finite-array identity
\[
\frac{\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})}{\sigma}
=\widehat x_F-h\mu_{a,N}\mu_{b,T}. \tag{16}
\]
The uniform profile theorem gives
\(\widehat x_F-x_\star(\eta,h)\xrightarrow{p}0\) uniformly on compact subsets of the bounded experiment.  The two moment assumptions give
\(\mu_{a,N}\mu_{b,T}\to\mu_a\mu_b\).  Substitution in (16) proves the asserted stochastic absorption law.

It remains to identify the phase exactly.  At the ATT coordinate
\(x_{\operatorname{ATT}}=h\mu_a\mu_b\), direct substitution in the two-by-two profile gives
\[
B_{\eta,h}(x_{\operatorname{ATT}})
=\kappa h
\begin{pmatrix}
0&\mu_a\sqrt{v_b}\\
\sqrt{v_a}\mu_b&\sqrt{v_av_b}
\end{pmatrix}. \tag{17}
\]
Sign changes of rows and columns are orthogonal transformations.  Therefore, with \(C_\eta\) from the absorption-phase definition,
\[
s_1\{B_{\eta,h}(x_{\operatorname{ATT}})\}
=\kappa|h|s_1(C_\eta). \tag{18}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\), \(\kappa>0\), \(v_a,v_b>0\), and
\(|\mu_a|,|\mu_b|>0\); thus \(s_1(C_\eta)>0\), so division in the definition of \(h_{\mathrm{crit}}\) is valid.

In the rotated scalar coordinates of the global singleton theorem, the point \(z=0\) is exactly
\(x=x_{\operatorname{ATT}}\), and its \(\tau(0)\) is the squared largest singular value in (18).  The theorem selects \(z_\star=0\) exactly when
\(\tau(0)^2\leq c\).  By (18), this condition is
\[
\kappa^4h^4s_1(C_\eta)^4\leq c
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
|h|\leq\frac{c^{1/4}}{\kappa s_1(C_\eta)}
=h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta). \tag{19}
\]
This includes \(h=0\) and equality at the spectral edge.  If the inequality is strict in the opposite direction, the global singleton theorem gives
\(0<z_\star<z_0\) and
\[
x_\star=\frac{\operatorname{sgn}(h\mu_a\mu_b)}{\kappa}(z_0-z_\star),
\qquad
h\mu_a\mu_b
=\frac{\operatorname{sgn}(h\mu_a\mu_b)}{\kappa}z_0. \tag{20}
\]
The two strict signed inequalities in the statement follow immediately from (20).

All entries of \(C_\eta\), the largest-singular-value map, \(c^{1/4}\), and \(\kappa\) are continuous on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\); the denominator in (19) is bounded away from zero there.  Hence \(h_{\mathrm{crit}}\) is continuous and positive.  The strict inverse image defining \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\) is therefore relatively open.  Compactness of \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\) implies that
\(h_{\mathrm{crit}}\) attains its minimum.  If \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\neq\varnothing\), its defining inequality gives
\(\overline h>\min_\eta h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta)\).  Conversely, if this strict inequality holds, take a minimizing \(\eta_0\) and choose
\(|h|\in(h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta_0),\overline h]\); then
\((\eta_0,h)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\).  This proves the claimed equivalence without adding a signal-reach assumption.
